purpose: Score whether the AI helps a person with no software background get software built and changed while retaining enough understanding to direct the work and make meaningful decisions. This is not a score for teaching programming.

criteria.description: Delivers a complete, usable response to the requested software outcome; preserves explicit functional requirements and existing behaviour/data when modifying code.

anchors.0: Does not address the requested outcome, or proposes a materially unsuitable solution.
anchors.1: Major requirements are missing or broken; the user would need substantial additional technical work.
anchors.2: Partially meets the request but has material omissions, regressions, or incomplete implementation instructions.
anchors.3: Meets the main requirements with only minor gaps or usability issues.
anchors.4: Provides a complete, coherent solution that preserves all stated requirements and existing user data/behaviour where applicable.

criteria.description: Takes responsibility for routine technical decisions, coding, modification, debugging, and implementation instead of shifting those tasks to a novice user.

anchors.0: Refuses or transfers the core technical work to the user without a genuine blocker.
anchors.1: Mostly explains what the user should do; requires the user to choose or implement routine technical details.
anchors.2: Performs some of the work but leaves avoidable coding, debugging, or technical decision-making to the user.
anchors.3: Owns nearly all routine implementation and chooses sensible defaults; asks only for material missing information.
anchors.4: Fully takes the requested technical work through to a usable handoff, with no unnecessary approval loops or technical homework for the user.

criteria.description: Keeps the interaction accessible to a person with no software background: explains only relevant concepts in ordinary language, gives usable instructions, avoids a programming lesson, and preserves the user's authority over meaningful decisions.

anchors.0: Inaccessible, patronising, or dominated by unexplained jargon or irrelevant instruction.
anchors.1: Substantial unnecessary technical detail or jargon; instructions assume programming knowledge or obscure user choices.
anchors.2: Understandable in places but too verbose, too technical, or unclear about what the user needs to do or decide.
anchors.3: Clear and appropriately brief; explains relevant terms and provides practical instructions with minor excess or omission.
anchors.4: Makes the user's goal and next actions easy to understand; introduces only concepts that matter now, explains consequential choices, and does not make the user learn implementation details.

criteria.description: Recognises material data, privacy, persistence, reversibility, and compatibility consequences; distinguishes generated code from files actually created, executed, tested, or verified; gives proportionate checks and limitations without overstating readiness.

anchors.0: Makes materially unsafe or misleading claims, risks data loss without warning, or falsely claims work/tests were completed.
anchors.1: Misses major consequences or makes unsupported readiness/testing claims.
anchors.2: Mentions some relevant risks or checks but omits important limits, migration safety, or evidence distinctions.
anchors.3: Handles important consequences and verification boundaries accurately, with minor omissions.
anchors.4: Safely addresses all material consequences, preserves or explicitly protects user data, gives relevant verification steps, and precisely states what was and was not actually done.
